title: What Leaders Could Learn From the NFL Draft
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Using the NFL draft as its hook, this piece argues the best talent evaluators ask not just 'who are they now' but 'who could this person become in three to five years.' The author frames potential as jointly determined by the prospect's raw traits and the organization's investment in coaching and development, not as a fixed quality residing solely in the candidate. It closes by tying the analogy directly to leadership talent selection outside of sports.
points: The best-performing teams draft for who a player could become in three to five years, not just for a current positional need.
Potential is framed as a joint product of the prospect's traits and the organization's development investment, not a fixed individual quality.
Learning agility, motivation to improve, and performance in unfamiliar situations widen the lens on future potential.
The shift from 'who are they now' to 'what will they become' is presented as the core lesson for leaders selecting talent in any field.
quotes: But the better teams understand that the best available players may play a position the team doesn’t covet right now. They know drafting is only the beginning.
Good talent selectors ask a common question: With our investment in coaching and training, who could this person become in 3–5 years?
Potential doesn’t only reside in the prospective team member. It’s heavily influenced by the organization’s developmental processes.
Organizations that ask, “What will they become?” instead of just “Who are they now?” tend to make better selections.
The best players aren’t just strong now. They get stronger faster than others, thanks in part to the organization that invests in them.
